title: Delhi Ministers Order Half Their Staff Home as Air Stays Very Poor
excerpt: Delhi's overall AQI was 348 on Saturday morning, down from Friday's 24-hour average of 373 and Friday morning's reported 494 peak, as two ministers applied a 50 per cent work-from-home cap in their departments.
body:
• The newest step: Delhi ministers Manjinder Singh Sirsa and Pankaj Kumar Singh have directed their departments to run a 50 per cent work-from-home arrangement, under a Winter Action Plan in force since November 1, with essential services exempt.
  • Delhi's overall AQI stood at 348, in the 'very poor' category, at 9 a.m. on Saturday, November 14, according to CPCB data reported by The Hindu BusinessLine, compared with a 24-hour average of 373 at 4 p.m. on Friday.
  • Seven of the city's 59 monitoring stations still recorded 'severe' air on Saturday morning; ANI reported North Campus at 421, IIT Delhi at 419 and ITO at 415 at around 7 a.m.
  • These figures are not the same reading as Friday's peak: ANI reported the overall AQI touching 494 at 7:31 a.m. on Friday, November 13. The Air Quality Early Warning System forecasts further deterioration in the next few days.

Delhi's government has moved to cut office attendance as the capital's air stayed 'very poor' on Saturday morning, November 14. Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa and Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh directed their respective departments to implement a 50 per cent work-from-home arrangement, intended to reduce the number of vehicles travelling to government offices while essential services continue without disruption.

Saturday's reading, in its own terms

The overall Air Quality Index stood at 348 at 9 a.m. on Saturday, in the 'very poor' category, according to data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) reported by The Hindu BusinessLine. The same report put Friday's 24-hour average AQI at 373 at 4 p.m. Under CPCB standards cited in that report, an AQI of 301 to 400 is 'very poor' and 401 to 500 is 'severe'.

ANI, reporting CPCB data recorded at about 7 a.m. on Saturday, gave the same overall figure of 348 and named the stations still in the severe zone: North Campus recorded 421, IIT Delhi 419, ITO 415 and Burari Crossing 410. Chandni Chowk recorded 392 and Jawaharlal Nehru University 390, both 'very poor'. The Hindu BusinessLine reported that seven of the city's 59 monitoring stations recorded 'severe' AQI on Saturday morning. Station readings differ between reports because they were recorded at different times; they are separate snapshots, not a single citywide number.

What the work-from-home direction actually covers

The directions apply to the two ministers' respective departments, not automatically to every office in the capital. They follow Delhi's Winter Action Plan, which came into effect on November 1 and includes a provision to cap physical attendance of government employees at 50 per cent. Under the plan, administrative secretaries and heads of departments are required to attend office regularly, with no more than half the staff strength physically present, and department heads can call officials in whenever necessary for essential and emergency services.

For a Delhi government employee in those departments, the practical position is therefore specific: expect to work from home under the 50 per cent cap, unless your head of department calls you in for essential work.

Friday's peak, and a dispute over the data

Saturday's 348 follows a worse Friday morning. ANI reported that Delhi's overall AQI touched 494 at 7:31 a.m. on Friday, November 13, with dense fog and pollution reducing visibility, and CPCB station readings that morning included IIT Delhi at 488 and ITO at 455. That 494 is a Friday morning reading; it should not be read alongside Saturday's 348 as if both described the same hour.

The figures themselves are now contested. AAP leader Saurabh Bharadwaj, citing a report by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, alleged that pollution data had been manipulated and that actual levels were 49 per cent higher than officially displayed, ANI reported. That is an allegation by an opposition leader, reported as such; the reports carried no CPCB response to it. Separately, ANI reported that the Commission for Air Quality Management ordered GRAP Stage 3 restrictions in the NCR and adjoining areas on November 6, and that the Delhi government has been deploying water sprinklers. Sirsa said on Wednesday that cloud seeding trials were ongoing under the supervision of IIT Kanpur, according to ANI.

What to watch

According to forecasts by the Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi reported by The Hindu BusinessLine, the AQI is expected to deteriorate further in the next few days. That forecast, Saturday's seven severe stations, and the new departmental work-from-home directions together describe the current position: a modest easing from Friday's peak on the citywide average, severe air persisting in parts of the capital, and the government using attendance caps to cut traffic while the episode continues.
